title: Astro Burn brings its cat-powered cute-em-up to iOS after launching on Android
summary: I think cute-em-ups were always at their best when they made slightly less sense than they should. Astro Burn understood that assignment, and after a month on Android, the shooter is now available on iOS too. If the term’s new to you, it’s the old arcade shooter with the grimness swapped out for cartoons. Beyond the Pixels is pointing straight at Parodius and Pop’n TwinBee for inspiration, Konami’s 90s shooters where you could fly as a penguin or an octopus and nobody batted an eyelid.  ... [MORE]

title: Collapse Protocol pits you against the bureaucratic mess that is the afterlife
summary: Work - it's what takes up the majority of our lives, for better or for worse. But in the world of the afterlife, your work isn't just what's keeping you fed and watered; it's also what's keeping the scales of reality balanced. So, your new job as the probationary intern working for the afterlife is just that in Collapse Protocol. No pressure. At its core, Collapse Protocol is essentially just Papers, Please in the afterlife. You take up the role of probationary clerk, meeting the recently deceased and deciding where they end up, be that Heaven, Hell or Purgatory. That means finding out from their file what they were like in life, how they died and hearing their argument for where they should go. ... [MORE]

title: Qwak Reborn brings the classic platformer back to mobile in all its chaotic glory
summary: While international fans can chart the history of gaming via consoles pretty easily, the early days of PC were very different. And over in the UK, we had our own miniature indie scene that produced some very strange takes on classic genres, like chaotic platformer Qwak. Now, in Qwak Reborn you'll step into the challenging platforming once again, this time on iOS and Android! Qwak Reborn is a deceptively simple platformer with a single objective: get your heroic duck to the end of each level. But as you'll see from the store page and gameplay below, this is far from as simple as it sounds as you dodge obstacles, gather power-ups and take out foes on the way to the exit. ... [MORE]

title: Vampire Therapist lets you guide your immortal f(r)iends through eternity using psychology
summary: Who wants to live forever? Despite how often classical heroes strove for it, I think most people agree that immortality isn't all it's cracked up to be. Especially not if you're an ageless, blood-feeding creature of the night... erm, not that I would know! But in Vampire Therapist you'll guide similarly dysfunctional immortals through the trials and tribulations of unlife. In the critically acclaimed Vampire Therapist, you play a reformed, former Wild West gunslinger now using their immortal experience to help others of their kind. Whether it's a vampire from Iron Age Ireland, Renaissance-era Italy, Tudor England or beyond, you'll get to know them and also help them work through their emotional struggles when it lands on iOS and Android come November 24th! ... [MORE]

title: Roco Kingdom launches its first closed beta test for the latest iteration of Tencent's hit franchise
summary: During my time at Gamescom 2026 earlier this year, one of my more pleasant surprises was Roco Kingdom. What I'd initially dismissed as just another Palworld-like turned out to be an open-world ARPG with more going for it than just creature collecting. Now, potential fans can get their hands on it for the first time as Roco Kingdom's first closed beta goes live! The Quack Quack closed beta (yes, really) will see you step into the world of Carosia to meet the various inhabitants, including magical creatures known as Jinies. These Jinies will fight on your behalf, and even lend their incredible abilities to navigating the world of Carosia and uncovering its secrets! Catherine certainly enjoyed dipping in for her Roco Kingdom preview! ... [MORE]

title: Fieldrunners 2 receives surprise update for the first time in almost a decade
summary: One unfortunate reality of mobile is that many of the hits we enjoyed as kids have slowly slipped into obscurity, forgotten by devs and long since incompatible with modern operating systems. But sometimes, they buck the trend with a surprising comeback, which is exactly the case with Fieldrunners 2! Longtime readers may remember Fieldrunners 2 being a cornerstone game we covered extensively during the 2010s. After last receiving an update in 2018, Subatomic Studios' popular tower defence game has come roaring back into the limelight, receiving new towers, missions, maps and events, not to mention being remastered for high-resolution screens! ... [MORE]

title: Pokémon Unite is shutting down in March 2027, days after its final tournament
summary: Pokémon Unite’s biggest tournament of the year now has its finals booked for two days before the servers go dark. The Pokémon Company and TiMi Studio Group have announced that the MOBA is ending service on both mobile and Switch, so whoever wins the Aeos Crown 2027 in Tokyo gets to keep the title for good. The esports side shouldn’t come as much of a shock if you were following along over the summer. Back in July, Pokémon confirmed Unite wouldn’t be part of the 2027 Championship Series or the World Championships, with the Tokyo event spun off as its own thing. So, August’s Worlds in San Francisco ended up being its last appearance there.  ... [MORE]

title: How Many Dudes? set to drop major new update and seven new dudes this month
summary: Having sold over 300,000 copies already across multiple platforms, developer Butterscotch Shenanigan's chaotic battle sim How Many Dudes? still isn't done answering just that question. In the new 1.1 update, arriving October 29th for all platforms, you'll have seven new dudes at your disposal, willing to throw their lives away battling all manner of strange opponents. If you're not already familiar, How Many Dudes? is based on the viral concept which asked people to propose how many regular people it would take to defeat a gorilla in hand-to-hand combat. Butterscotch Shenanigans took the concept even further, throwing not just gorillas, but wolves, gods and even bloodthirsty toddlers at you! ... [MORE]

title: Bills Must Be Paid, the piggy bank smashing sim, now has a release date for mobile
summary: Ready for a smashing good time? In Bills Must be Paid, the incremental game from developer Rike Games, you can do just that. Smash piggy banks to get cash, try not to tire yourself out, fail anyway and come back stronger (at least in the hand department). You may recall we covered Bills Must Be Paid a few weeks ago, and Tanish seemed to be enamoured with its curious mix of incremental game mechanics and Balatro-style roguelite progression. title: Fortnite coming back to the iPhone App Store in Australia following another defeat for Apple
summary: After more than half a decade since it first started, the Apple v Epic saga is still grinding on, although now only in a very perfunctory manner. And the latest big defeat for the iPhone maker has been in Australia, where the courts have forced Apple to follow the example set by other markets and open its storefront to third-party apps. Of course, that also means Fortnite is now going to be available on iOS in Australia, officially, once more! This follows the change mentioned above, and the introduction of other shifts in policy, such as allowing alternative payment methods for in-app transactions, and whatnot. ... [MORE]

title: Playdigious announces iPhone Duo compatible games, including Subnautica and Planet of Lana
summary: The iPhone Duo is already making headlines around the world, both for good (the innovative design) and for bad (the massive price tag). But it's undoubtedly proving to be popular, with many owners now wondering which of their mobile games are compatible with the new device. A question Playdigious looks to answer. title: Kettle Street brings British life sim chaos to Android, complete with nosy neighbours and butties
summary: Three years of living in the UK has prepared me for a worrying amount of Kettle Street. It’s a cosy British life sim out now on Android. You’ve just moved into a bare flat in a small town called Kettleby. Maureen at number 11 has already put the kettle on. title: Mika: Dungeon Backpacker makes you pack the heroes’ bags before sending them into danger
summary: If I’m playing a game called Mika: Dungeon Backpacker, I’d expect her to be the hero of her own story. Except she really isn’t. She’s a Dungeon Supporter, which as far as I can tell means she packs everyone’s bags while four heroes take the credit. It’s a backpack-building roguelite with grid-based dungeons, and it’s coming soon to iOS and Android. The setting is Stonia, a continent that’s slowly turning into dungeons, and Mika’s latest job takes her into the ruins of a cathedral where an expedition disappeared a century ago. Something has been asleep down there ever since. Cheerful stuff. ... [MORE]

title: Dispatch brings choose-your-own superhero shenanigans to mobile this winter
summary: Who wouldn't want to be a superhero? Fly through the air, bend steel with your bare hands, or any variety of other crazy powers. But while the fantasy may be fun, there's a less glamorous side of superheroism when you really think about it, which is precisely what Dispatch does as it comes to mobile this December 9th! You play as Robert, formerly Mecha Man, who joins the Superhero Dispatch Network when his suit is destroyed and must wrangle a group of oddball, would-be superheroes into an effective crime-fighting force. Dispatch is the hit, choose-your-own-adventure style narrative game that sees you navigating an atypical office job while guiding your team of heroes to fight crime and save people. ... [MORE]
